children.objective: Use the row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update as the primary experiment: compare its contiguous B/C traversal and compiler vectorization with the original r-c-k loop, first with a simple serial variant. If search results warrant it, test row-parallel, unrolling, or other correctness-preserving variants as separately measured follow-ups; distinguish traversal gains from those added changes. Stay within the caller’s thread budget. Check overwrite behavior and the fixed oracle tolerance on all official sizes, compare repeated native n=1024 timings, and record unsuccessful variants.
children.subject: Row-major r-k-c streaming, vectorization, and thread interaction

children.objective: Make OpenMP decomposition and scaling the primary question. First establish a controlled parallel speedup using the existing r-c-k dot-product traversal, with disjoint output ownership; compare sensible row or output-region partitions, scheduling, and thread counts up to min(threads, 8). Avoid overhead on small inputs when measurements justify it. After this anchor is measured, correctness-preserving kernel changes may be explored as explicit interactions; record whether a timing change came from scheduling, thread count, or kernel order. Validate all official sizes and record failed variants.
children.subject: OpenMP work partitioning and thread scaling

children.objective: Use a blocked GEMM with a register-oriented output microkernel as the primary approach. Measure simple blocking separately from optional packing, explicit SIMD, and parallel tile ownership so gains and regressions can be attributed; include packing and scratch allocation in timed cost. Where useful, compare C initialization by zeroing once against safely overwriting on the first reduction block. Use only compiler/ISA mechanisms supported by the frozen target, respect the caller’s thread budget, and preserve the fixed FP32 tolerance and complete overwrite on every call. Validate all official sizes, compare repeated native n=1024 timings, and record unsuccessful variants.
children.subject: Blocked GEMM, packing, and register microkernels
